title: Why he left Basie and Basie's reluctance to play new arrangements
summary: Durham found Basie more interested in a good time than business or writing; Basie avoided odd arrangements, so Durham pushed Buck Clayton's charts.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, why did you leave Basie?
I left Basie because I had been with Lunceford. And Lunceford's band was so polished, society-type wise, --
And I thought Basie wasn't being business enough. Basie was always -- he always wanted a good time with me, he didn't want to do any writing.
And I said -- I just left that .
The band, though, was improving at this time, wasn't it?

Yeah. Well, I said I'll be here a year, and that's as long as I stayed. It seemed like it wasn't moving fast enough for you, you see. Because I was out to write and play, and Basie wanted a good time a lot. "This is your band, just like me, you ain't supposed to --" He'd go into one of those things, and, boy.

And we used to with Benny Moten and say, someday we're going to have our own band, and we're going to set in a car and ride. The bus would be in front of us, and "there's my Cadillac," and I'd say yeah, well, I ain't waiting for you tonight. And that's the way he thought. He say, you ain't supposed to be over here working, you're supposed
to be having a good time.
But he, now -- Basie at that point, he wanted to keep -- I take it he wanted to keep the arrangements sort of fairly simple, didn't he?
I mean, he didn't want anything sort of ambitious.
No, he didn't care about way out stuff.

Because, like, if anybody brought arrangements around that was a little odd, he didn't want to play it. And the only way (inaudible) play it. And Buck was writing nice. And he wouldn't play Buck's arrangements. And a lot of time when he'd be getting ready to call the numbers, I would tell him to play these two numbers Buck did yesterday, and that's how they got playing. So Buck's numbers got played like that. And so I was the instigator.
